description:
Ready to let AI pore over your medical records? Claude and ChatGPT are already doing it, and now Microsoft’s Copilot is ready to review your chart.

Copilot Health is a “separate, secure space” within the Copilot app that “makes sense of your information” from a variety of health-related sources, from your Apple Watch and Oura ring to uploaded lab results, and medical records from your doctor, Microsoft says.

As with ChatGPT Health and Claude’s health integrations, Copilot Health isn’t designed to “replace” your doctor, Microsoft carefully notes. Instead, it’s intended as a way to sort through reams of medical data and turn it “into a coherent story,” allowing you to “arrive prepared, with the right questions” for your actual doctor visits.

title: Now Copilot wants to check your vitals, too

description:
Microsoft has begun rolling out KB5079473, a new update that adds a number of features to Windows 11.

We’ve already highlighted some of these new features back when we looked at the preview of this update, which included features like the new Sysmon security tool, improvements to Windows Backup, Quick Machine Recovery (QMR), and the new “built-in” speedtest.

Other features include the ability to use WebP image files as desktop backgrounds and support for R
title: Windows 11 just got a bunch of new features with March’s update

description:
In 2026, figuring out how to watch baseball is more confusing than ever.

MLB teams are switching channels on cable and satellite TV as regional sports networks collapse, while new companies are carving up the rights for games on national television. New streaming services are also coming online for watching in-market games without blackouts, even as ESPN has introduced more complications for watching out-of-market games on MLB.TV.

I can’t make the situation any simpler, but as someone who covers the streaming space pretty closely, I can at least lay out the options in a way that makes sense. Here’s how to navigate the baseball streaming options as opening day approaches:
title: MLB and ESPN blew up baseball streaming. Here’s help
